title: [finding] The `#3521` note "the RECORD HEADER does not speak CEL" looks stale against the pinned ActionEngine — needs a browser confirmation before anyone acts on it either way
body:
Filed unassigned by the `pm-dispatch` seat of the `objectstack` repo, as the cross-repo half of **objectstack#8990** (PR objectstack#9280). Recording only — not claimed, not queued.

⚠️ **Provenance, stated up front: I did not measure this myself.** It comes from the `os-dev` agent that migrated the showcase's authored action predicates. I am filing it because the measurement is specific and consequential and would otherwise exist only inside a PR body in another repo — but the "confirm in a browser" step below is genuinely outstanding, and nothing here should be acted on as settled.

## The note in question

A comment in the `objectstack` showcase's `predicate-matrix.action.ts` carries an `objectui#3521` bullet asserting:

> The RECORD HEADER does not speak CEL

If that is true today, it is load-bearing in a dangerous direction. objectstack#8990 has just migrated **51 header-located gates** to the `has(...)` guard, and `has()` **throws** in objectui's legacy JS evaluator — measured directly: `SafeExpressionParser` answers `"has" is not a function`. A header that routed to that evaluator would therefore have every one of those 51 gates silently vanish, which is a strictly worse version of the fail-closed bug the migration exists to fix.

## Evidence that it is stale, read at the PINNED sha

The reporting agent read `objectui` at **`665661ab`** — the sha `objectstack` actually pins, fetched specifically because the local checkout sat on a different commit:

- `ActionEngine.getActionsForLocation` passes a `{dialect: 'cel'}` envelope **INTACT** to `evaluateCondition`, which routes it to `@objectstack/formula` (per objectui#2661 / objectui#3314).
- In the built artifact, **113 of 114** record-scoped predicates in `dist/objectstack.json` are `{dialect, source}` envelopes, because `defineAction` normalizes the shorthand at build time.

So on that reading the action face is CEL on every surface, `has()` is safe, and the `#3521` bullet describes a state that no longer holds.

## Why the note was NOT rewritten

The agent had **no browser/preview tooling** in its session, so it could not confirm behaviourally and deliberately left the comment alone rather than editing a note it could not verify. That was the right call and I want it preserved as such: the evidence above is **static** — it reads code and a build artifact, not a running header.

⭐ One piece of independent, non-static evidence does exist and is worth weighing: all three `Dogfood Regression Gate` shards passed on objectstack PR #9280, and those shards boot the example apps and exercise real user flows. That is behavioural evidence against the "header throws on `has()`" hypothesis, which is why that PR was allowed to land. It is not the same as someone opening the header and looking.

## What would close this

1. Open a record-detail page in a running app and confirm the header's action gates evaluate on CEL (a `has()`-guarded gate resolves rather than disappearing).
2. Then either **correct or delete** the `#3521` bullet in `objectstack`'s `examples/app-showcase/src/ui/actions/predicate-matrix.action.ts` — it is a comment in the other repo, so the fix lands there, but the fact it asserts is this repo's.
3. If the bullet turns out to be **true** for some surface after all, that is urgent rather than cosmetic: say which surface, because objectstack#8990's migration assumed otherwise across 51 gates.

## Related

objectstack#8990 (the migration) · objectstack PR #9280 (where this was measured) · objectstack#9167 (the `record:alert` page-block face, whose fault DIRECTION is separately unmeasured — objectui#4807 records it as fail-soft) · objectui#2661, objectui#3314 (the CEL routing) · objectui#3521 (the note's origin) · objectui#4807
